To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dental team should be flexible in their approach to dental examinations for children with autism, and that parents should have confidence to advocate for their child's needs.

parents of children with an autism spectrum disorder or a working diagnosis of autism have positive and negative dental care experiences and that the dental team should be flexible in accommodating their needs.

the dental care of children with autism can be improved by the dental team providing flexible appointments in a relaxed environment, being aware of hyper empathy and communicating effectively with parents and children with autism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of a positive dental team-parent relationship in order to support children with autism in primary care dental services.
the experiences of parents and children with autism in accessing dental services, and how these can be improved.
the experiences of parents of children with an autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and how they perceive the dental services for their child.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a strong relationship between the parents and the whole primary care dental team is essential to enable children with autism to receive dental examinations and have a satisfactory experience of care.

the experiences of parents of children with Autism and/or working diagnosis of Autism can provide valuable insight into the issues surrounding accessing and receiving dental care and how these issues can be improved.

the dental team should work in partnership with the parent, to provide a flexible, safe and child-centred dental environment, with continuity of care, clear communication and clear referral pathways for those children who need specialist dental treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a strong relationship between the parents and the whole primary care team is essential for the children with autism to be able to access and receive dental examinations.
the parents' experiences highlight the importance of a family centred approach, with the dental team being flexible, responsive and empathic to the needs of the child and family.
the dental team should have the flexibility to adapt the environment and approach to suit the needs of the child and their family.
The main takeaway from our work is that

dental professionals should not assume that parents are not able to communicate their child's needs and advocate for them, and should not be reluctant to treat these children because of a lack of knowledge about autism.
the dental environment can be made more autism friendly by the use of visual supports and clear communication with parents.
parents are key partners in care and their views should be taken into account in service design and development.
